headline: Six of seven majors above their 200-day line, RSI stretched, and whales quietly reversing weeks of exchange deposits
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's lopsided in a way that matters: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages, and ETH, SOL, and BNB carry golden crosses (the 50-day above the 200-day, a longer-run trend confirmation). DOGE and ADA are the outliers, both still under their 200-day lines despite double-digit monthly gains of 25.8% and 31.6%. That's a market where the majority of capital is trending up on the long timeframe while two well-known names haven't repaired the technical damage yet. One asset below the 200-day is noise; two out of seven is a genuine split worth watching rather than ignoring.

Momentum is where the story gets interesting. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 72, BNB at 72.4, both in territory usually read as overbought, and BTC's MACD is still above signal (accelerating, not resting). But look at the daily print: BTC is down 0.3% on the day even as it's up 3.2% on the week and 24.6% on the month. That's a market that ran hard and is pausing, not reversing, at least not yet. ETH tells a different, quieter story: RSI at 67.8, price up 0.2% on the day, but MACD has crossed below signal even as the golden cross holds. Trend says up, short-term momentum says cooling. That divergence is a finding, not a flaw, and it's the kind of thing that shows up before a range starts, though what happens after a pause is not something the tape tells you in advance.

Positioning adds texture. BTC funding on OKX is a modest 0.0053% per 8 hours (5.8% annualized), cheap by crypto standards, and open interest sits near $2.39B. But BTC's long/short account ratio is 0.89, meaning more accounts are short than long even as price grinds higher, an odd mismatch that liquidation data explains: over the trailing 3 hours, shorts got liquidated for $208,708 versus $77,730 in longs, so the shorts caught the wrong side of a small squeeze. ETH funding runs hotter at 11% annualized with a long/short ratio of 1.11, and its 1-hour liquidation window shows shorts eating $457,427 against just $11,619 in longs, a sharper squeeze. Compare that to SOL, where funding is negative (-3.4% annualized, shorts paying longs to hold) and the long/short ratio is a lopsided 1.94, or DOGE at 3.37, both signaling a crowd leaning long on the smaller names even as DOGE sits under its 200-day. Crowded and cheap is one thing; crowded and stretched is another, and DOGE's combination of a heavy long tilt with price still below trend is worth flagging.

Flows tell a supply story that lines up with the ETF bid. BTC spot ETFs posted a $730.8M net inflow on 03 Sep 2026, with the five-session net at $610.2M, both pointing the same direction, so this is more than a one-day blip. ETH ETFs added $141.4M on the same day, $291.5M over five sessions. On the whale side, the last 48 hours show $27.0M net moving off exchanges in BTC, a small number, but it comes after three straight weekly prints of coins moving onto exchanges (Aug 14: $813M onto, Aug 21: $380M onto, Aug 28: $1,185M onto) followed by the week ending Sep 04 flipping to $275M net off exchanges. That's a trend reversal in the whale data worth naming, and it's paired with a large single move: $203.3M in USDC left Coinbase Institutional in this window, alongside BTC transfers off the same venue, suggesting institutional wallets repositioning rather than retail panic. Stablecoin float is up 1.45% over 30 days to $310.3B, dry powder building slowly rather than surging.

Sentiment sits at 74, Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 74. That's the crowd feeling good, and on the majors the price action mostly agrees with them. But BTC's short-heavy positioning ratio and DOGE's long-crowded, below-trend setup both show pockets where the tape and the crowd aren't perfectly aligned. What to watch from here: whether the weekly whale flow (off-exchange for the week ending Sep 04) holds for another week or reverts to the onto-exchange pattern seen in the three prior weeks, whether BTC's RSI above 70 resolves into a pause or a deeper pullback, and whether ADA and DOGE manage to reclaim their 200-day lines given their strong monthly gains are running without that trend confirmation underneath them.
